24 A bicycle gear wheel is a disc with 50 ‘teeth’ equally spaced around its edge, as shown. The gear
wheel is rotated 10 times each second. A springy strip of metal is vibrated by the rotating ‘teeth’.
The metal strip produces a sound of frequency that is equal to the frequency of vibration of the
strip.
gear wheel
fixed clamp
springy strip
of metal
teeth
The speed of sound in air is 330 m s–1.
What is the wavelength of the emitted sound?
A
0.66 m
B
1.5 m
C
6.6 m
D
500 m

hints: Count how many teeth hit the springy strip in one second when 50 teeth pass on each of the 10 rotations per second.
Link that tooth-strike rate to the vibration frequency of the strip and hence to the frequency of the emitted sound wave.
Use $v = f\lambda$ with $v = 330\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to find $\lambda$, checking that frequency is in Hz and wavelength is in metres.
walkthrough: Each rotation brings 50 teeth past the springy strip, and the wheel makes 10 rotations each second.
So the number of strikes per second is $50 \times 10 = 500\text{ s}^{-1}$, giving vibration frequency $f = 500\text{ Hz}$ and sound frequency $500\text{ Hz}$.
For the sound wave, $v = f\lambda$, so $\lambda = v/f$.
Substitute $v = 330\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $f = 500\text{ Hz}$: $\lambda = 330/500 = 0.66\text{ m}$ with unit metres.

A.explanation: With $f = 500\text{ Hz}$ and $v = 330\text{ m s}^{-1}$, $\lambda = v/f = 0.66\text{ m}$.

B.explanation: 1.5 m is close to $f/v$ instead of $v/f$, which inverts the wave equation.

C.explanation: 6.6 m results from using only 10 teeth per second and ignoring the 50 teeth per revolution.

D.explanation: 500 m is the vibration frequency in Hz, not the sound wavelength in metres.
